links.label: his rookie partner
links.evidence: BEOM SUNG-HOON is Dong-jin's rookie partner

links.label: refuses the Kingfisher story he once chased — he knows something
links.evidence: He can't seem to tear himself away from investigation updates, but he also refuses to cover the Kingfisher story himself.

links.label: the righteous cop on Kingfisher's tail; every lead slips through his fingers
links.evidence: Dong-jin is determined to catch Kingfisher, one way or another. The trouble is, every time he gets any sort of lead, it slips right through his fingers.

links.label: friends practically all their lives; Tae Seong was there when Dong Jin's parents were murdered
links.evidence: He and Tae-sung have been friends practically all their lives. Tae-sung was there for Dong-jin during their school years when Dong-jin's parents were murdered

links.label: her friend — with a crush he does not see; judo athletes both
links.evidence: BEOM SUNG-HOON is Dong-jin's rookie partner, and he doesn't seem to realize he has a bit of a crush on his best friend.

links.label: her mentor, now a florist
links.evidence: …a direct trail from the kid whose father Seul-gi shot to the flower shop Bo-na's mentor owns to Bo-na herself.

links.label: mother-in-law who makes her do the memorial table alone and calls her 'the orphan'
links.evidence: Sun-ja calls Bo-na to help prepare the family memorial table. And by 'help,' I mean Bo-na does all the work while Sun-ja looks for things to criticize.

links.label: childhood friend from Russia; fired in front of a child on her hit — she banished him
links.evidence: Seul-gi smooth-talked her into letting him 'line up the shot' and then pulled the trigger before she could stop him. Furious, Bo-na told him to leave and never come back.

links.label: the girl Bo Na saved from her father on Christmas, fifteen years ago; tests her with a fake poisoning, then devoted
links.evidence: Remember the girl Bo-na saved from her abusive father fifteen years ago? That's Hyun-nam.

links.label: in love with her since the day she held a 'gun' to his head
links.evidence: Assistant Manager KI YOUNG-DO is nursing an obvious crush… He's carried a torch for Bo-na since the moment he first laid eyes on her

links.label: stands up to his mother for Bo Na; the memorial rite is abolished
links.evidence: He rebukes his mother, calling her and his sisters out for making Bo-na do their work, and declares that Bo-na is every bit as precious to him as he is to them.

links.label: operative of another vigilante team, met over a double target at the casino
links.evidence: …they all work for the same vigilante organization, with each team assigned to a different region… their volatile part-timer MOON DA-RAE

links.label: found him bleeding in a stairwell eight years ago and called the ambulance — he never knew; then the hospital roof, then the snowed-in lodge
links.evidence: She used his phone to call an ambulance, and to this day Tae-sung remains unaware he later married his anonymous savior.

links.label: a jealous, spur-of-the-moment date; a judo throw wins him over; they part in the end
links.evidence: He asks Se-ah on a date. It's a very spur-of-the-moment, jealousy-induced kind of decision

links.label: the 'Kingfisher' who kidnapped him four years ago and threatened his wife and child — the reason he stopped chasing the story
links.evidence: …he confesses that he knows who Kingfisher is: a tall man who kidnapped him and threatened harm to Tae-sung's wife and child if Tae-sung didn't back off Kingfisher's case for good.

links.label: murdered his parents; paroled early; shot by Kingfisher while Dong Jin hesitates
links.evidence: Eun-hak is his name, and his victims were Dong-jin's parents… And while he hesitates, Kingfisher does it for him.

links.label: Kingfisher shoots his parents' killer in front of him — he stakes his career on the task force
links.evidence: Seeing Eun-hak get gunned down completely wrecks Dong-jin… Dong-jin seizes upon a singular goal — to catch and punish Kingfisher — and stakes his entire career on it.

links.label: connects the dots — the flower shop, a soda can, her voice on an old recording; 'do you really love me?'
links.evidence: Bo-na's voice on that old recording is just the final nail in the coffin. Once that connection is made, there's no way for Tae-sung to stop his journalist brain from connecting all the remaining dots.

links.label: children of the same abuse compound, taken away by the same woman
links.evidence: …we get flashbacks to a whole compound of abused kids, Bo-na and Tae-min among them.

links.label: her new working-mom friend — a celebrity cop on the Kingfisher task force
links.evidence: Mi-ran happens to be Bo-na's new working mom friend, but up till now we've been led to believe she was an ordinary office worker.

links.label: the Kingfisher task force, together
links.evidence: This year, however, something is different: they have Dong-jin and celebrity cop YOO MI-RAN.

links.label: comes around after Bo Na stops the scammer who nearly took her savings
links.evidence: Sun-ja doesn't quite get a verbal 'thank you' out, but she does give Bo-na extra meat at dinner and even lets Tae-sung do the dishes.

links.label: a thing, on the side
links.evidence: …the Hyun-nam/Tae-min thing

links.label: chooses her side — a family outing with a flawless alibi; a half-truth to Dong Jin
links.evidence: As for Tae-sung, he's chosen a side. He suggests a family outing that weekend, and his smile returns.

links.label: raised her after the compound; heads a Russian vigilante group; never gave up on her
links.evidence: Bo-na was raised by her savior: a woman known simply as MAMA, A.K.A. Seul-gi's actual mother.

links.label: mother
links.evidence: a woman known simply as MAMA, A.K.A. Seul-gi's actual mother

links.label: her unseen guardian angel, appointed by Mama — back to stop Layla
links.evidence: Mama freely let Bo-na go, but never gave up on her and appointed Seul-gi as Bo-na's unseen guardian angel.

links.label: kicked out of Mama's fold; the copycat sniper out for revenge — shoots her in the park
links.evidence: Layla hates that Bo-na is living happily on the moral high ground… Bo-na throws herself in front, taking the bullet in her shoulder.

links.label: lets Kingfisher 'die' with Layla rather than reopen the case — friendship wins
links.evidence: …friendship wins out in the end, as he chooses to let Kingfisher die with Layla rather than keep looking for evidence that might reopen the case.

links.label: finds her in the mountains, over the field he once showed her; wants to know all of her now
links.evidence: He wants to know everything now — the good, the bad, the frightening — so he can come to love every last part of her.

links.label: secretly buys her the chicken shop
links.evidence: Sun-ja finally gets to own her chicken shop instead of renting it, though I wonder if she'll ever find out the generous landlord was Bo-na.
